_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 5 $84A9-$87E3: the status screen's open ($801B), close ($801E), the HUD weapon icon ($8033) and the ATTACK/SHIELD pips. The inline strings and the tables $84C3, $85DA, $8690, $87E4 are claimed elsewhere. The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: Clear the status screen's nametable, part 1: its attributes
regions.description: `JSR $C06C` (`$D5CC`) with four inline bytes `40 27 C0 00`: 64 bytes of `00` at PPU `$27C0`, the whole attribute table of nametable 1 (physical `$2400`: the status screen is drawn there, and so is the HUD). The call returns past the inline bytes, so execution carries on at `$84B0`. Called by the open (`$84DA`) and the close (`$8738`). RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate. After the close all 64 attribute bytes of nametable 1 are zero.

regions.name: Clear the status screen's nametable, part 2: the rows
regions.description: `$14` := `$20` (the blank tile), `$15` := `$24` (nametable 1), `$17` := `$1C`, `$16` := `$18`, then `JMP $C084` (`$E453`, which clears rows `$17` up to `$16`-1 and wraps past row 29 to row 0): **rows 28, 29 and 0-23** of nametable 1. Rows 24-27 are left alone: that is where the HUD lives (25 SC/CHIP/SHOT, 26 the life meter, 27 AREA/X/Y). `$E453` returns to the caller of `$84A9`. RUN: after the close, rows 0-23, 28 and 29 of nametable 1 are all `$20`. RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Open: interrupts off, rendering off, save the palette
regions.description: STATUS SCREEN, OPEN (slot `$801B`, called from `$E500`): `SEI` (the DMC-timer IRQ that makes the HUD split is held off; this routine never clears the I flag, the close does), `JSR $C00F` (`$D4C1`: NMI off in `$FF`, rendering off in `$FE`), then the 24 palette bytes `$0181-$0198` are copied to `$04D0-$04E7` (the fade-target buffer, borrowed as a save area; `$0180`, the backdrop, is not saved). The close copies them back. RUN: after open + close the palette RAM equals the one before. RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Open: clear the screen, save sprite 0, hide the sprites
regions.description: `JSR $84A9` clears nametable 1. `$0177` := the Y of sprite 0 (`$0200`, the HUD split's marker, `$BF` in play), which the close puts back. `JSR $C015` (`$D534`) sets all 256 bytes of OAM to `$F8`: every sprite off screen, so the status screen starts with none (the entrance markers and the player's marker are added at the end of the open).

regions.name: Open: scroll and nametable
regions.description: `$FC` (the vertical scroll shadow) := `$B4` = 180 and `$A2` (the nametable select the NMI writes) := 1. Line 180 of the 240-line nametable is in row 22, so the screen's first visible rows are the bottom rows 28-29 of nametable 1 and then, wrapping, rows 0 on down: that is why the screen is built from rows 28, 29, 0-23 and why the 'KEY' row (29) sits above the key icons (rows 0-1). There is no raster split here (sprite 0 is hidden).

regions.name: Open: the palettes
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$84C3` and `JSR $C05D` (`$D92D`, the palette-list walker): background palettes 0-2 := palettes 5, `$0F`, `$1F` of the 36 at `$B30A`, background palette 3 skipped (`$FF`, it keeps the play palette), sprite palettes 0-3 := palettes 0-3. Table at `$84C3`.

regions.name: Open: the marker colours, and upload both palettes
regions.description: `$0196` := `$16` and `$0197` := `$30`: the first two colours of sprite palette 3 (`$0196-$0198`) become red and white (the third, `$0198`, stays `$0F`), the colours of the map's entrance and player markers. `$017F` := 3: upload both background and sprite palettes (bits 0 and 1; see the palette-upload entry in the RAM map). RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate. Palette RAM after the open ends `... 16 30 0F`.

regions.name: Open: load the map's quadrant tiles
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$1010`, A := 3, Y := 2, `JSR $C042` (`$D7F9`): arm the decompressor with **block 3 of bank 2** (the block at bank 2 `$959F`, 240 bytes = 15 tiles) for PPU `$1010-$10FF`: background tiles `$01-$0F`. Tile k is the map's quadrant tile: each of its four 4x4-pixel quadrants is filled when the matching bit of k is set (1 top left, 2 top right, 4 bottom left, 8 bottom right), colours 1 and 2, tile 15 solid. The map drawer `$891F` picks the tile by OR-ing those bits. RUN: all 15 tiles decoded from the ROM equal the live CHR after the open, and each tile's four quadrant fills equal its bits. RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Open: the frame tile (tile $00)
regions.description: `JSR $C06F` with a 19-byte inline PPU string `10 10 00` + 16 bytes: tile `$00` of pattern table 1 (PPU `$1000`) := plane 0 all `00`, plane 1 `FF 80 80 80 80 80 80 80`: colour 2 along the top row and the left column. It is the map frame's line tile (and is also the first key-door picture's tile `$00`: the close rebuilds that).

regions.name: Open: the word KEY
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `03 27 B0` + 'KEY': the label at PPU `$27B0`, row 29 column 16 of nametable 1 (the top row of the screen, over the key icons).

regions.name: Open: draw the map, then start the weapon icon upload loop
regions.description: `JSR $8805` first: the world map (the frame table `$87E4`, then the map itself; the next stretch). Then Y := 0 and `$19:$18` := `$1800`: the loop that uploads the 12 weapon icons.

regions.name: Open: upload one weapon icon
regions.description: Save `$18`, `$19` and Y on the stack, then a far call (inline `02 02 80`) to bank 2 `$8003` (-> `$81B2`, the icon uploader) with A = Y: icon Y of the 18 at bank 2 `$8E0C` (four 2-bpp tiles, 64 bytes) goes to PPU `$19:$18`. RUN: the 12 icons 0-11 at `$1800 + 64 k` equal bank 2 `$8E0C + 64 k` in the live CHR after the open.

regions.name: Open: weapon icon loop
regions.description: Restore Y and the pointer, add `$40` to it (the next icon's 64 bytes), Y++; repeat until Y = 12: PPU `$1800-$1AFF` holds the 12 weapon icons.

regions.name: Open: start the key icon loop
regions.description: Y := 1 and the same save/far-call shape, now to bank 2 `$8006` (-> `$8212`, the key-icon builder, inline `02 05 80`) with A = Y = the key number 1-7: PPU `$1B00 + 64 (k-1)`, so `$1B00-$1CBF` hold the seven key pictures (the pointer carries on from `$1B00`, where the weapon loop left it).

regions.name: Open: key icon loop
regions.description: Restore, pointer += `$40`, Y++, loop until Y = 8 (seven keys).

regions.name: Open: the level pips
regions.description: A far call (inline `00 17 80`) to bank 0 `$8018` (-> `$8034`): a `JSR $C06F` with 35 inline bytes that write 32 bytes at PPU `$1CC0`: **tiles `$CC` and `$CD`**, the two small pictures that the ATTACK and SHIELD rows repeat once per level (`$CD` for attack, `$CC` for shield). RUN: `$1CC0-$1CDF` equal those 32 bytes after the open.

regions.name: Open: the slot loop (20 slots)
regions.description: `$16` walks the 20 slots of the table `$8690` in steps of 4 (Y = `$16`): slots 0-6 are the keys, slot 7 (Y = `$1C`) is the zero slot and is skipped, slots 8-19 are the 12 weapons. Each slot: the cell to draw at `[ppu lo][ppu hi]`, its attribute address and its tile.

regions.name: Open: a key slot - owned or not
regions.description: Y below `$1C`: n := Y/4 (key n+1), `JSR $C078` (`$EFC7`, bit n -> mask), AND `$04B0` (the keys held): A := 1 if the key is held, else 0; pushed. (The weapon branch is the `BCS` at `$8596`.) RUN: with `$04B0` = `$55` keys 1, 3, 5, 7 were drawn and 2, 4, 6 blank.

regions.name: Open: a weapon slot - its level
regions.description: Y above `$1C`: weapon number := Y/4 - 8 (0-11; the `LSR`s leave carry clear, so the `SBC #$07` subtracts 8), `JSR $C075` (`$E498`: the 2-bit level of that weapon from `$04AC-$04AE`, 0-3, 0 = not owned); pushed. The first `$18`/`$19` stored here (the slot address with the row ORed with `$20`) are overwritten at `$85C7`: dead stores.

regions.name: Open: draw the slot's picture
regions.description: A (the key flag, or the weapon level) indexes `$85DA`: `$17` := `00 00 55 AA` = the attribute pattern mask (keys always 0; weapons level 0-1 palette 0, level 2 palette 1, level 3 palette 2). `$18`/`$19` := the slot's PPU address. The pushed value is pulled: zero (key not held, weapon not owned) draws tile `$20`, the blank; otherwise the slot's own tile (`$8693,Y`).

regions.name: Open: draw one 16x16 cell and step to the next slot
regions.description: Tile in A, the slot's attribute address (`$8692,Y`) in Y, `JSR $C054` (`$D865`): queue a 2x2 cell at PPU `$19:$18` with that tile as base, the attribute byte at the given address updated with the pattern mask `$17`. The four tiles go in the order base, base+2 (top row) and base+1, base+3 (bottom). Then `$16` += 4; at `$50` (20 slots) the loop ends, else `JMP $858D`. RUN: with weapon levels `$04AC` = `E4`, `$04AD` = `1B`, `$04AE` = `C1` the owned weapons showed their slot tile and the others blank. RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Open: 'NO' for the weapon window
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `02 2D C2` + 'NO': PPU `$2DC2` (row 14, column 2). With the next string, 'USE' at row 15, it is the default text of the A-button weapon window; what the per-frame handler `$8937` does with it when a weapon is selected is the next stretch.

regions.name: Open: 'USE'
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `03 2D E2` + 'USE': PPU `$2DE2` (row 15, column 2).

regions.name: Open: is the Enemy Eraser owned?
regions.description: `$04AE` AND `$C0` (weapon 12's two level bits): zero skips to `$8625`; otherwise `JSR $C06F` with inline `02 2E 50` + 'EE': the label for the Eraser's stock at PPU `$2E50` (row 18, column 16).

regions.name: Open: the Eraser's stock
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$2E70` and A := `$04AF` (the stock), `JSR $C051` (`$E1CD`): three blank-suppressed digits at row 19, column 16. RUN: `$04AF` = 7 gave 'EE' over '  7'.

regions.name: Open: 'CHIP MAX'
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `08 2C 90` + 'CHIP MAX': PPU `$2C90` (row 4, column 16).

regions.name: Open: the chip maximum
regions.description: `$17:$16` := `$4E/$4F` (CHIP MAX), `$19:$18` := `$2C99`, `JSR $C04E` (`$E24B`, the four-digit printer: left-justified, blanked zeros, 9999 cap). RUN: `$4E` = 50 printed '50' at row 4, column 26.

regions.name: Open: the ATTACK and SHIELD rows
regions.description: `JSR $8782` (ATTACK) and `JSR $879F` (SHIELD): a label and a row of level pips each.

regions.name: Open: 'WEAPON POWER'
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `0C 2D 30` + 'WEAPON POWER': PPU `$2D30` (row 9, column 16). The number beside it is written by the per-frame handler.

regions.name: Open: 'USE CHIP'
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `08 2D 50` + 'USE CHIP': PPU `$2D50` (row 10, column 16). The number beside it is written by the per-frame handler.

regions.name: Open: the weapon's power and chips per use
regions.description: `JSR $89CB`: prints the selected weapon's level `$3D` (one ASCII digit, PPU `$2D3D`) and the chips per use `$45` (three digits at `$2D5B`), the numbers beside WEAPON POWER and USE CHIP. **CORRECTION: an earlier version of this note called `$89CB` 'the map's markers'; the entrance markers are drawn by `$8805`'s own loop.** It is also called by the per-frame handler (`$89BF`).

regions.name: Open: sprite tables, and remember the weapon
regions.description: `$FF` := (`$FF` AND `$DF`) OR `$08`, written to PPUCTRL: 8x8 sprites (bit 5 clear) from pattern table 1 (bit 3), the table whose tile `$01` is the map's marker. `$0176` := `$3C`, the selected weapon, for the close to compare. RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate. PPUCTRL `$B1` became `$99`.

regions.name: Open: start the cursor repeat counter, blink the marker
regions.description: `$15` := 5 and `$14` := 0, then a far call (inline `02 1D 80`) to bank 2 `$801E` (-> `$8998`), the blinking player marker (it writes the last four sprites, OAM `$02F0-$02FF`, one pattern per call; it reads neither `$14` nor `$15`). **CORRECTION: the 5 and 0 are not arguments of `$8998` (the first version of this note called them a lead): `$15` is the cursor handler's auto-repeat counter, read only by `$8946`, so a direction held from before the screen opened waits 5 frames; `$14` is not read by the handler.** The marker sits at (column x 4 + `$10`, row x 4 + `$3B`) = (`$30`, `$6B`) for position (8, 12).

regions.name: Open: picture on
regions.description: `JMP $C063` (`$EDF4`): wait for the vertical blank, NMI on, two frames, rendering on (`$D4D5`). It does not execute the `CLI` of `$EDF2`: after the open the I flag is still set (RUN: P = `$24`).

regions.name: HUD SHOT icon: blank
regions.description: `JSR $C06F` with a 9-byte attribute-cell item `C7 3C 20 20 20 20 F7 00 FF`: the 2x2 cell at PPU `$273C` (nametable 1 row 25, column 28, right of the word SHOT) gets four blank tiles `$20`, attribute address `$F7` (`$27F7`), mask `00`, pattern `FF`. The item layout is the one `$D865` writes: `[C0 | hi][lo][t0][t1][t2][t3][attr address lo][mask][pattern]`.

regions.name: HUD SHOT icon: return
regions.description: RTS of the blank case.

regions.name: REFRESH THE SHOT ICON IN THE HUD (slot `$8033`)
regions.description: Called by the close (`$8715`), by `$89BC` in the per-frame handler and, through the slot, by the weapon cursor code in other banks. `$3C` zero: `BEQ $86E0` draws the blank cell. Otherwise `JSR $C06F` with the item `C7 3C 3C 3E 3D 3F F7 00 FF`: PPU `$273C`, tiles `$3C $3E` over `$3D $3F`, the four tiles that `$86FD` uploads the weapon's icon to. RUN: weapon 3 -> after the NMI drained the queue, nametable 1 rows 25-26 columns 28-29 read `3C 3E / 3D 3F`; weapon 0 -> `20 20 / 20 20`.

regions.name: SHOT icon: upload the weapon's picture
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$13C0` (tiles `$3C-$3F` of table 1) and A := `$3C` - 1, a far call (inline `02 02 80`) to bank 2 `$8003` (the icon uploader): icon (weapon - 1) of the 18 at bank 2 `$8E0C` becomes the HUD's weapon picture. (The queue item has been written first; the NMI drains both.) Not verified byte for byte: the harness's NMI had not drained the upload when read.

regions.name: SHOT icon: return
regions.description: RTS.

regions.name: STATUS SCREEN, CLOSE (slot `$801E`, called from `$E50F`): off, and refresh the SHOT icon
regions.description: STATUS SCREEN, CLOSE (slot `$801E`, called from `$E50F`): `SEI`, `JSR $C00F` (NMI and rendering off), `JSR $86ED` (the HUD's weapon icon for the weapon as it is now). RUN: bank 5 live, `$84CB` then `$8711` called on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Close: a different weapon was chosen
regions.description: `$3C` compared with `$0176` (the weapon on entry). **Different:** `JSR $C048` (`$CCBF`, remove an object) for slots 3 and 4, the A-button weapon's objects, and unless `$30` bit 3 is set (the launch/landing flight) `JSR $C069` (`$F726`, load the sprite tiles of the selected weapon). Same: skipped. RUN: weapon 3 -> 5: `$CCBF` called for slots 3 and 4, `$F726` called, and the sprite tiles changed; 3 -> 3: neither called.

regions.name: Close: HUD uses-left, sprites off, clear the screen
regions.description: `JSR $C072` (`$E1C3`) reprints `$3E`, the uses left, in the HUD; `JSR $C015` hides all sprites; `JSR $84A9` clears nametable 1.

regions.name: Close: sprite tables back
regions.description: `$FF` := (`$FF` AND `$F7`) OR `$20` to PPUCTRL: 8x16 sprites, sprite table 0 again.

regions.name: Close: reload the scene
regions.description: `LDA $5C / JSR $ACA9`: load the current scene again (tile blocks to the background CHR, metatile sets, palettes) - this overwrites the status screen's CHR at `$1000-$1CDF`. **`$30` bit 6 set (a corridor):** also scene 1, the corridors' common scene, then `JMP $8760`. Clear (the labyrinth): carry on at `$8757`. RUN: corridor close called `$ACA9` with `$5C` then 1 and did not call `$ED51`.

regions.name: Close, labyrinth: key-door pictures
regions.description: `JSR $C08A` (`$ED51`): rebuild the key pictures for this room's exits in background tiles `$00-$07` (see the key-door entry). RUN: with exits (3, 8, 8, 5) tiles `$00-$03` equal the key-3 icon built on its own after the close, `$04-$07` hold key 5's; with no key doors tile `$00` keeps the frame tile (harmless: no key door is drawn).

regions.name: Close, labyrinth: the eight glyphs
regions.description: A far call (inline `02 0B 80`) to bank 2 `$800C` (-> `$8153`): the font record set 1, eight glyphs into background tiles `$08-$0F` (PPU `$1080-$10FF`), which the map's quadrant tiles had replaced. Together with `$ED51` this restores tiles `$00-$0F`. RUN: after the close CHR `$1080-$10FF` equals its value before the open.

regions.name: Close: restore the palette
regions.description: `$04D0-$04E7` are copied back to `$0181-$0198` (the copy the open made).

regions.name: Close: upload the palette, wait for the tiles, commit the scroll
regions.description: `$017F` := 3 (both palettes), `JSR $C045` (`$D7C3`: wait for the decompressor), `JSR $C087` (`$E522`: write the scroll variables back to the shadow registers, which restores `$FC` and the nametable select from `$A6`-`$A9`). RUN: after the close `$FC` = 0, `$A2` = 0 as before.

regions.name: Close: one object-loop pass
regions.description: A far call (inline `06 FF 7F`) to bank 6 `$8000`, the object loop: every object runs once and draws its sprites into the OAM the open emptied. That is the reading of why it is here; the caller `$E515` does one more pass after the close returns.

regions.name: Close: sprite 0 back, picture on
regions.description: `LDA $0177 / JMP $C060` (`$EDE5`): `JSR $D51E` sets sprite 0's Y from A (the HUD split's marker), then the code falls into `$EDE8`: DMC rate `$87`, `$EDF4` (vblank sync, NMI on, two frames, rendering on), **`CLI`** - the interrupt flag the open set is cleared here (RUN: P `$24` after the open, `$21` after the close).

regions.name: ATTACK row: the label
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `06 2C B0` + 'ATTACK': PPU `$2CB0` (row 5, column 16).

regions.name: ATTACK row: its pips
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$2CB7`, `$15` := `$CD` (the pip tile) and A := `$4A`, the attack level, then `JMP $87B9`.

regions.name: SHIELD row: the label
regions.description: `JSR $C06F`, inline `06 2C D0` + 'SHIELD': PPU `$2CD0` (row 6, column 16).

regions.name: SHIELD row: its pips
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$2CD7`, `$15` := `$CC` and A := `$4B`, the shield level; falls into `$87B9`.

regions.name: Level pips: nothing to draw
regions.description: A (the level) zero: RTS.

regions.name: Level pips: queue a run of A tiles
regions.description: `$C04B` (`$D6D3`) waits until the PPU queue has room for A + 3 bytes, `$C03C` (`$D6E0`) reserves the entry; the entry is `[A][hi $19][lo $18]` followed by A copies of the pip tile `$15`, and `JMP $C03F` (`$D6F7`) commits it. RUN: attack level 2 -> two `$CD` at row 5 columns 23-24; shield level 3 -> three `$CC` at row 6 columns 23-25.
